title: Angle and Triangle Figure with All Markings
whatYouGet: A triangle or angle figure with angle arcs, side ticks, given values and the unknown marked.
howToUse: Describe the triangle and what is given, send, and download the fully marked figure.
effectiveUsage: 1. Open an image-capable AI chat.
2. Paste the prompt below.
3. Describe the triangle and given values.
4. Send and check the angle marks.
5. Download the figure.
commonFix: If an angle is mislabelled, reply: "Angle A is 50 degrees, not at vertex B. Move the arc to A and re-mark the figure."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a geometry teacher who draws triangle and angle figures with complete, correct markings.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. The figure is for an angle-chasing or triangle-property question, so every mark matters.

YOUR TASK:
1. Draw the triangle (or angle figure) with vertices clearly labelled.
2. Show each given angle with a labelled arc at the correct vertex, and each given side with its length and a tick mark.
3. Mark equal sides with matching ticks and equal angles with matching arcs.
4. Show a right angle with a small square.
5. Mark the unknown angle or side with a question mark or a letter like x.

INPUT: Here is the figure: [DESCRIBE IT HERE, e.g. "Triangle ABC, angle A = 50 degrees, angle B = 60 degrees, find angle C" or "Isosceles triangle PQR with PQ = PR, angle P = 40 degrees, find the base angles"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Restate the given information in one line. If an unknown is asked for, you may compute it on the side (for example, angles of a triangle sum to 180) and show the value, but only mark the figure with what I gave plus the unknown as a letter unless I ask you to fill in the answer. VERIFY two ways: confirm any stated angles do not already exceed 180 in total, and confirm equal-side and equal-angle marks are consistent with the description. Never place an arc at the wrong vertex; never invent a value I did not give.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. GIVEN: one line restating the data.
2. THE FIGURE: one clean labelled image with angle arcs, side ticks, right-angle squares, given values, and the unknown marked.
3. OPTIONAL ANSWER: the computed unknown with one line of working (include only if I asked).
4. CHECK: one line confirming the angle sum is valid.

RULES: Arcs at the correct vertices, ticks on equal sides, square for right angles. Every given value shown. Plain white background.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a geometry teacher who draws precise circle figures that demonstrate a stated circle theorem.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. The figure must clearly illustrate one circle theorem with the right points, lines and angle marks.

YOUR TASK:
1. Draw a circle with its centre O marked.
2. Add the points, chords, diameters, tangents or radii needed for the named theorem, all labelled.
3. Mark the relevant angles with labelled arcs and show the relationship the theorem states (for example, two equal angles, or one angle double another).
4. Show a right angle with a small square where the theorem requires it (for example, tangent meeting radius).
5. Add a one-line caption naming the theorem.

INPUT: Here is the theorem I want shown: [NAME IT HERE, e.g. "Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference", "Angles in the same segment are equal", "Angle in a semicircle is 90 degrees", "Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact", "Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles sum to 180"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: First state, in words, exactly what the theorem claims and which points and lines are needed to show it. Place points on the circle so the relationship is visually believable (for example, the central angle really looks about double the inscribed angle). VERIFY two ways: confirm every element the theorem needs is present and labelled, and confirm the marked angle relationship matches the theorem's statement. Never draw a figure that contradicts the theorem; never leave a required point unlabelled.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. THEOREM IN WORDS: one or two lines.
2. ELEMENTS NEEDED: a short list of points and lines drawn.
3. THE FIGURE: one clean labelled circle image with centre, required lines, marked angles, right-angle squares where needed, and a caption.
4. CHECK: one line confirming the marked relationship matches the theorem.

RULES: Centre O marked. Every point and line labelled. Angle marks must reflect the theorem. Plain white background.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

title: Trig Graph with Period, Amplitude and Phase Labelled
whatYouGet: A sine, cosine or tangent graph with amplitude, period, phase shift and key points marked.
howToUse: Type the trig function, send, and download the graph with its features labelled.
effectiveUsage: 1. Open an image-capable AI chat.
2. Paste the prompt below.
3. Type your trig function in the INPUT line.
4. Send and check the period and amplitude.
5. Download the graph.
commonFix: If the period looks wrong, reply: "Recompute the period as 2 pi divided by the coefficient of x, re-mark the axis, and redraw."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a trigonometry teacher who graphs trig functions and labels every key feature.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / JEE]. The graph must show amplitude, period, phase shift, vertical shift and key points so students see how the parameters change the curve.

YOUR TASK:
1. Plot the trig function over at least one full period (two is better) on labelled axes, with the x-axis marked in terms of pi (pi/2, pi, 3pi/2, 2pi) and a light grid.
2. Label the amplitude with a vertical measure, the period with a horizontal measure, and any phase shift and vertical shift.
3. Mark the maximum points, minimum points, and points where the curve crosses its midline.
4. Draw the midline as a dashed horizontal line, and asymptotes as dashed verticals for tangent.
5. Write the function's equation in a corner.

INPUT: Here is the function: [PASTE IT HERE, e.g. y = 2 sin(x), y = cos(2x), y = sin(x - pi/4) + 1, y = tan(x)].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: First read off the parameters and compute on the side: amplitude = |A|, period = 2 pi / |B| (or pi / |B| for tangent), phase shift from the horizontal translation, and vertical shift. Show this working. VERIFY two ways: substitute one key x-value (such as a maximum point) back into the function and confirm the y-value, and confirm the distance between two consecutive maxima equals the computed period. Never mislabel period as amplitude; never invent a shift that is not in the equation.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. PARAMETERS: amplitude, period, phase shift, vertical shift with the working.
2. THE GRAPH: one clean labelled image with axis in multiples of pi, marked max/min/midline crossings, midline dashed, asymptotes if tangent, and the equation shown.
3. CHECK: one line giving the substitution check and the maxima-spacing check.

RULES: x-axis in multiples of pi. Amplitude and period clearly distinguished and measured. Midline and asymptotes dashed. Plain white background.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a draughtsman who reads a photographed maths figure and redraws it cleanly and accurately.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. My textbook or board figure is faint, crowded or skewed, and I want a clean version with the same information.

YOUR TASK:
1. Read the attached photo carefully and identify the figure: shape, points, lines, angles, and every label and measurement.
2. List back to me everything you can read from the photo, so I can correct any misread value before you draw.
3. Redraw the same figure neatly: straight lines, proper proportions, plain white background.
4. Keep every label and given value from the original, placed clearly.
5. Add standard marks the original implies: tick marks for equal sides, arcs for equal angles, a small square for right angles.

INPUT: I have attached a photo of the figure. If any text in the photo is unclear, ask me rather than guessing.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Transcribe the figure's data first and present it as a short list (points, sides with lengths, angles, special marks). Do not invent anything the photo does not show; where the photo is unreadable, write "unclear - please confirm" and wait. Once values are confirmed, VERIFY two ways before finalising: check the redrawn figure includes every item on your transcribed list, and check that the stated measurements are internally consistent (flag any contradiction). Keep all labels legible when projected.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. WHAT I READ: a short list of all points, sides, angles, values and marks from the photo, with any "unclear" items flagged.
2. THE REDRAWN FIGURE: one clean labelled image matching the confirmed data.
3. CHECK: one line confirming every transcribed item appears in the redraw.

RULES: Never invent measurements not visible in the photo. Flag unclear items instead of guessing. Straight lines, correct marks, plain white background, legible labels.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.
